debian.source: Dockerfile.base / Dockerfile.development / Dockerfile.production FROM ruby:3.4.12-slim-trixie (Phase 14; Phase 13 had moved the Ruby tag on Bookworm first so the two bumps bisect separately)
debian.toolchain: apt 3.0.3, gcc 14.2.0 (build-essential 12.12), libpq-dev / libpq5 17.11, zlib1g-dev 1.3.1, liblzma-dev 5.8.1, curl 8.14.1, patch 2.8 — every apt package name the Dockerfiles install exists unchanged on Trixie; /etc/apt/sources.list.d/debian.sources is deb822 format (no apt-key, nothing in the Dockerfiles uses it)
debian.notes: slim-trixie is the minimal Debian 13 variant shipped with the official Ruby Docker image (tags exist for Ruby 3.2+ only). Predecessor Debian 12 Bookworm left regular security support on 2026-07-11 (LTS to 2028-06-30) and its OpenSSL 3.0 passed upstream EOL on 2026-09-07. GCC 14 turns -Wincompatible-pointer-types into an error, so 2018-era C extensions fail to build (byebug 10 in PR #229); every native extension in the Phase 13 lock compiled on Trixie in Phase 14. Since Phase 7 the pg gem bundles its own libpq (18.6) and OpenSSL, so Trixie's libpq-dev 17 is only a source-build fallback. Successor: Debian 14 Forky (no release date yet).

openssl.debian_trixie_package: openssl / libssl3t64 3.5.7-1~deb13u3 (OpenSSL 3.5.7 9 Jun 2026; patch level tracks Trixie point releases)
openssl.ruby_openssl_ext: ruby:3.4.12-slim-trixie's openssl gem 3.3.3 reports OpenSSL::OPENSSL_LIBRARY_VERSION 'OpenSSL 3.5.7 9 Jun 2026'
openssl.notes: OpenSSL 3.5 is the current LTS line (supported to 2030-04-08) and keeps the 3.0 provider model, so the Phase 3 legacy-provider check still applies; legacy algorithms (MD5-based signatures, RC4, etc.) live in the legacy provider. Predecessor OpenSSL 3.0 LTS (Bookworm) passed upstream EOL on 2026-09-07 with Debian carrying fixes for Bookworm's remaining lifetime.
